title: Detection rules
intro: Sigma rules (YAML) from the rules/ directory – deployed with deploy.sh rules or a SigmaHQ import; the detector reloads them within 30 s. Every content change is a new version (history in the details). An administrator can disable or enable a rule from the panel – with a reason, recorded in the audit log. Correlation rules from the wizard are stored in the panel (file panel/…).
notConfigured: The detector (siem-detector) has not run yet – no rules loaded.
fileErrors: Files with errors ({{count}}) – these rules do not work

filter.search: search: title, id, file, tag (e.g. attack.t1059)

selectFilteredTitle: select all rules matching the filter ({{count}})
trialTip: Trial mode since {{date}} ({{by}}{{reason}}): hits without alerts, results in “Rule trials”.
overrideTip: Set in the panel: {{by}}, {{date}}{{reason}}. In the file: {{file}}.

delete.title: Delete rule “{{title}}”
delete.warning: The whole panel rule will be deleted (the correlation and its base rules from the same record). Version history and alerts are kept. Give a reason (recorded in the audit log) and confirm with your password.
delete.done: Deleted – the detector will stop evaluating the rule within 30 s.

toggle.trialInfo: In trial mode the rule counts hits (computers, days, last event) without alerts or notifications – results in “Rule trials”. After a week or two you can see whether it is safe to enable.
toggle.trialWarning: During the trial the rule will not raise alerts – not even for a real attack. Give a reason (recorded in the audit log) and confirm with your password.
toggle.disableWarning: A disabled rule will not raise alerts – not even for a real attack. Give a reason (recorded in the audit log) and confirm with your password.
toggle.reasonHint: e.g. false positives from the backup server until the rule is fixed
toggle.done: The change takes effect within 30 s (the detector reloads its rules).
toggle.doneTrial: Trial mode takes effect within 30 s – hits without alerts in “Rule trials”.

bulk.title: {{action}} – selected rules: {{count}}

info.trial: The rules will count hits without alerts or notifications (the “Rule trials” page). Enabled rules in the selection stop alerting during the trial.
info.enable: The rules will start creating alerts and notifications. Enabling many rules without a trial can flood analysts with false positives.
info.disable: Disabled rules will not raise alerts – not even for a real attack.
info.file: The rules return to the setting from their file (enabled in the rule); panel settings are removed.

bulk.skipInfo: Rules the change does not apply to (e.g. already in that state or built-in) are skipped. The change is recorded in the audit log; the detector applies it within 30 s.
bulk.reasonHint: e.g. reviewing SigmaHQ Windows rules before enabling them
bulk.done: Rules changed: {{changed}} (unchanged: {{skipped}}) – the detector applies the changes within 30 s.

tester.intro: The rule (YAML) is checked and run against events from ClickHouse – nothing is deployed or saved. Alerts are counted the same way as in the detector (grouping, thresholds). A changed rule is deployed as a file in the repository

trialsPage.intro: A rule in trial mode is evaluated on live events (streaming engine) but creates no alerts or notifications – it only counts hits since the trial started. Set trial mode on the rules page (one rule or the selected ones, e.g. all high-level SigmaHQ rules). Threshold rules count condition hits, without the threshold.
empty: No rule is in trial mode. On the
page select rules (e.g. SigmaHQ filter, high and critical level) and choose “Trial mode”.

short.label: too short
short.help: the trial has run for less than a day – wait for the result

quiet.label: quiet – safe to enable
quiet.help: no hits – the rule is not noisy on this data

rare.label: rare
rare.help: less than 1 hit per day – review the samples and enable

moderate.label: moderate
moderate.help: 1–20 hits per day – check whether these are real events, consider exceptions

noisy.label: noisy
noisy.help: more than 20 hits per day – without tuning it will flood you with alerts

trialsPage.gone: (the rule is no longer in the directory)
footer: Trials run in the streaming engine (
stream or both). Hits are kept for 35 days; restarting a trial counts from zero.

sigma.intro: is an open database of Sigma rules. Vardr supports a subset of Sigma – the import copies rules for the collected sources to rules/sigmahq/, drops the ones the parser does not support and deploys the rest disabled. On a server installed with the installer a single script is enough; from the Vardr repository – commands in the project directory. Details: docs/en/rules.md, “Importing SigmaHQ rules”.

serverSteps.title: Import or update the rules (on the Vardr server)
serverSteps.note: Downloads SigmaHQ from GitHub, copies rules for the collected sources, skips the ones incompatible with the parser and leaves all of them disabled. Upgrading Vardr keeps the imported rules.

repoSteps.title: Clone the SigmaHQ repository next to the project (update: git -C ../sigma pull)
Copy the categories for the sources we collect
repoSteps.note: When updating, remove the old rules/sigmahq directory first – rules enabled in the panel stay enabled (they are stored by rule id).

repoSteps.title: Remove the rules Vardr does not support (then repeat step 4 – 0 errors)
Disable all imported rules in their files
repoSteps.note: Otherwise hundreds of rules would be enabled at once after deployment.

sigma.after1: SigmaHQ rules are listed as disabled (file sigmahq/…) and do not load the detection.
sigma.after2: Check a chosen rule on the Test tab against 7 days of events; if there are no false positives, enable it with the switch. Enabling survives a re-import.
sigma.after3: A rule for events the agent does not collect will load, but the test shows 0 events.
sigma.licenseText: – use, modification and distribution are allowed provided the author (author field), source and license are kept. Do not remove the author and references fields from the rules.

wizard.title: Correlation wizard
wizard.intro: Pick sample events that together indicate an attack (e.g. an account created and then added to the administrators group). The wizard suggests steps, a common key and a time window, builds a Sigma Correlation rule and lets you test it on history before saving.

type.label: Type
type.temporal: all steps within the window, any order (temporal)
type.temporal_ordered: all steps within the window, in order (temporal_ordered)

v.title: enter a title
v.noFields: step “{{step}}”: select at least one field for the new base rule
v.threshold: step “{{step}}”: a threshold rule cannot be a correlation base – choose another or a new one
v.twoSteps: a temporal correlation needs at least two different steps
v.field: choose the field whose distinct values to count
v.key: the key does not match the steps – choose it again

yaml.baseDescription: Base rule of correlation “{{title}}” from the panel wizard.

wizard.searchPlaceholder: e.g. code:4720 or user:john or action:login outcome:failure
wizard.newFromFields: New rule from this event's fields
wizard.noMatching: no deployed rule matches this event – the wizard will create a base rule
wizard.fieldsHint: Select the fields that must match for an event to be this step (usually the event type, e.g. EventID, action, outcome – not the account or address, since the correlation key links those).
wizard.noSigmaProduct: Source without a Sigma equivalent – the rule selects events by the event.dataset field.
editNote: A correlation rule with its base rules (documents separated by
wizard.saved: Saved – the detector loads the rule within 30 s.
wizard.noPicks: None. Add events with the search below or in Mímir (event details → “Add to correlation wizard”). For a series of one kind (e.g. failed logons from many addresses) a few samples of the same event are enough.
wizard.missing: {{count}} of the selected events are no longer in the database (retention) – skipped.
wizard.stepsIntro: Each event is a correlation step: an existing rule that matches it or a new base rule from the selected fields. Events with the same choice form one step. Steps are ordered by the time of their first sample.
wizard.keyHintSteps: A value present in all steps – the wizard found it in the samples. Different field names in the steps are aliases.
wizard.keyHintOne: A value common to all samples – events with the same value are counted.
wizard.noKey: no key – all events together (rarely makes sense)
wizard.noCommon: The samples have no common value. Add events concerning the same account, computer or address.
wizard.valueField: Field whose distinct values to count
wizard.descriptionHint: what it detects and why it is dangerous
wizard.instructionsHint: fields of the last event ({{example}}) and {{vars}}
wizard.generate: Base rules still raise their own alerts (generate: true)
wizard.generateHint: off – base rules only feed the correlation
wizard.generateWarning: The correlation uses deployed rules. Without “generate” these rules will stop raising alerts on their own (unless another correlation needs them) – usually not what you want.
wizard.edited: YAML edited manually – changing the fields above overwrites it.
wizard.testNote: The generated rule (YAML) – you can edit it manually. “Test” counts the alerts that would have been raised on events from the selected period; nothing is saved.
wizard.adminOnly: Saving requires the administrator role – copy the rule and pass it to an administrator.

exceptions.intro: Events matching an exception do not trigger the rule (both engines). For recurring false positives – instead of disabling the whole rule.
exceptions.help: All fields must match. The same field several times = any of the values. Keep the condition as narrow as possible (e.g. computer and process) and check how many hits from the last 7 days it would hide before saving.
exceptions.aiDraft: Proposed by the AI assistant – check the condition against history and correct it before saving. An exception weakens detection.
exceptions.fromEvent: Add a field from the alert…
exceptions.checkResult_one: The exception would hide {{count}} hit from the last {{days}} days (alerts: {{alerts}}).
exceptions.checkResult_other: The exception would hide {{count}} hits from the last {{days}} days (alerts: {{alerts}}).
exceptions.reasonPlaceholder: e.g. nightly backup run by svc_backup
exceptions.deleteConfirm: Delete the exception? The rule will detect these events again.
exceptions.badgeTip: Active exceptions – details in the “Exceptions” tab.
exceptions.pseudonyms: The condition contains pseudonyms from AI data masking ({{list}}) – an exception needs real values. Reveal them or type the values yourself.
